```{r, echo=FALSE}
# filtering and recoding
df.final <- dplyr::filter(dfresult5, Remove == 0, Finished == 1, Status == 0)

df.final$List <- 0
df.final$List[grepl("PW",df.final$Target)]<-"PW"
df.final$List[grepl("PP",df.final$Target)]<-"PP"

df.1 <- dplyr::filter(df.final, df.final$List == "PP" & df.final$Order_PPList_Seen_First == 1)
df.2 <- dplyr::filter(df.final, df.final$List == "PW" & df.final$Order_PWList_Seen_First == 1)
df.3 <- dplyr::filter(df.final, df.final$List == "PP" & df.final$Order_PPList_Seen_First == 2)
df.4 <- dplyr::filter(df.final, df.final$List == "PW" & df.final$Order_PWList_Seen_First == 2)

df.1$Order_seen <- df.1$Order_Seen_First
df.2$Order_seen <- df.2$Order_Seen_First
df.3$Order_seen <- df.3$Order_Seen_First + 26
df.4$Order_seen <- df.4$Order_Seen_First + 18

df.final <- rbind(df.1, df.2, df.3, df.4)

df.final$List[grepl("PW",df.final$Target)]<-"PW" # move women from PP list to PW
df.final$List[df.final$Target == "PP14"]<-"PW"

df.final$RCorrect_recode <- 0
df.final$RCorrect_recode[df.final$RecallJob_coded == 1 | df.final$RecallName_coded == 1] <- 1

df.final$Power_centered <- df.final$Power_Composite - mean(df.final$Power_Composite)
df.final$Status_centered <- df.final$Status_Composite - mean(df.final$Status_Composite)
df.final$Power.Status.Scale_centered <- df.final$Power.Status.Scale - mean(df.final$Power.Status.Scale)

df.final$log.Rank <- log(df.final$Rank)
df.final$logMM <- log(df.final$Total.Media.Mentions)
df.final$logTF <- log(df.final$Number.of.twitter.followers)
df.final$logIF <- log(df.final$Number.of.followers)
df.final$List <- as.factor(df.final$List)

df.final$List <- recode_factor(df.final$List, `PP` = "Men", `PW` = "Women")
```

# KEY ANALYSES

# Multilevel models predicting Status Composite, Power Composite, and Power-Status Item
```{r, echo=FALSE}
m1 <- lmer(Status_Composite ~ List + (1 | idnum), data = df.final)
m2 <- lmer(Power_Composite ~ List  + (1 | idnum), data = df.final)
m4 <- lmer(Status_Composite ~ List + Order_seen + log.Rank + List*Order_seen + List*log.Rank + (1 | idnum), data = df.final)
m5 <- lmer(Power_Composite ~ List + Order_seen + log.Rank + List*Order_seen + List*log.Rank + (1 | idnum), data = df.final)
```

# Table 1
```{r}
tab_model(m1, m2, m4, m5, show.df = TRUE, show.stat = TRUE)
```

# Table 2
```{r}
m3aC <- glmer(Correct_Coded ~ List + (1 | idnum), data = df.final, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")) # list significantly predicts (less likely to recall list)

m10 <- glmer(Correct_Coded ~ List + Power_centered + Status_centered + List*Power_centered + List*Status_centered + (1 | idnum), data = df.final, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

m10b <- glmer(Correct_Coded ~ List + List*Power_centered + List*Status_centered + Power_centered + Status_centered + Order_seen + List*Order_seen + log.Rank + log.Rank*List  + (1 | idnum), data = df.final, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

tab_model(m3aC, m10, m10b, show.stat = TRUE, col.order = c("est", "ci", "stat", "p"), transform = NULL)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
# summary function for graphing
summarySE <- function(data=NULL, measurevar, groupvars=NULL, na.rm=FALSE,
                      conf.interval=.95, .drop=TRUE) {
  library(plyr)
  
  # New version of length which can handle NA's: if na.rm==T, don't count them
  length2 <- function (x, na.rm=FALSE) {
    if (na.rm) sum(!is.na(x))
    else       length(x)
  }
  
  # This does the summary. For each group's data frame, return a vector with
  # N, mean, and sd
  datac <- ddply(data, groupvars, .drop=.drop,
                 .fun = function(xx, col) {
                   c(N    = length2(xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm),
                     mean = mean   (xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm),
                     sd   = sd     (xx[[col]], na.rm=na.rm)
                   )
                 },
                 measurevar
  )
  
  # Rename the "mean" column    
  datac <- rename(datac, c("mean" = measurevar))
  
  datac$se <- datac$sd / sqrt(datac$N)  # Calculate standard error of the mean
  
  # Confidence interval multiplier for standard error
  # Calculate t-statistic for confidence interval: 
  # e.g., if conf.interval is .95, use .975 (above/below), and use df=N-1
  ciMult <- qt(conf.interval/2 + .5, datac$N-1)
  datac$ci <- datac$se * ciMult
  
  return(datac)
}
```
